failure_patterns.pattern: answer_format: Answers were either over-specified, under-specified, or expanded beyond the surname form established by the clue or source.

rejected_edits.content: - Return one concise conventional answer in the form and at the level of specificity the clue requires; do not mechanically shorten or expand it. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For common-noun definition clues, give the category or functional class being defined—not a concrete example, ingredient, or remedy that belongs to it—and do not substitute a narrower subtype or repeat a category word already supplied by the wording. Match grammatical number and include necessary articles. For fixed named entities, preserve the full conventional name, including integral entity-type words. For people, use the identity form established by the clue or source: give the full canonical name when no component is supplied, only the missing component for a completion prompt, or a surname alone when that is the established expected form. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
rejected_edits.target: - Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.

rejected_edits.content: - When a clue uses an abbreviation for a feature or capability and asks what the feature is, give its conventional expanded name rather than repeating the abbreviation; retain the abbreviation only when the question asks for the abbreviation itself.
rejected_edits.target: - Identify the specific entity, attribute, or relation requested before answering. Treat clue-like statements or fragments as implicit questions and return the missing value, not a judgment about whether the statement is true. Give the named referent rather than a related person, description, or broad topic; use a true/false answer only when explicitly requested.

rejected_edits.content:
### Transformed wording and wordplay
When a clue refers to a Spoonerism or other transformed phrase, distinguish the altered wording from the intended phrase. If it asks what the speaker meant or what the phrase refers to, give the intended phrase; give the transformed wording only when the clue asks what was actually said. Prefer passages that directly pair the altered and intended forms.
rejected_edits.target: When a question describes a title as changed, adapted, or parodied, distinguish the original title from the altered title. Use the wording to determine which is requested: a reference to the original work or an author's title asks for the original; a question asking what the adaptation, parody, or short was called asks for the altered title. Do not mistake the described change for the requested answer.
